subject: Clarify: Eval kickoff & benchmarking action plan for Claritywell
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex@claritywell.com>, Maya Singh <maya@claritywell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery — Claritywell eval kickoff

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap and proposed action plan so we have alignment on scope and what Redwood will run for the model-fit evaluation.

Call recap (high-level)
- Goal: establish which Redwood model(s) meet Claritywell's triage/QA assistant constraints (factuality + concise answer style) and produce a benchmarking report with recommended model and config for pilot.
- Target eval scope: ~1,000 labeled test prompts initially (goal: 500–2,000), stratified by triage type (diagnostic-summarization, medication-check, policy-advice).
- Data sensitivity: some prompts may contain PHI. Alex noted Claritywell will flag and tag PHI rows; need to confirm whether they require Private deployment or hosted with stricter retention.

Recommended Redwood baseline models for this run
- rw-instruct-13B (float16, default kernels) — strong instruction-following baseline
- rw-chat-7B-q4 (int8 quantized) — cost-conscious variant for throughput comparison
- opt-6.7b-instruct (reference) — an external comparator model (if you want a cross-vendor baseline)

Proposed evaluation metrics and rubric
- Automatic metrics: Exact Match (EM) for short, deterministic answers; ROUGE-L for longer outputs; BLEU as secondary where appropriate.
- Human review: 1–5 adequacy scale (accuracy/clinical safety), and a binary 'unsafe/needs escalation' flag.
- Regression guardrail: any >5% drop in human adequacy vs. baseline triggers manual review and rollback.

Deliverables Redwood will provide
- A runnable eval script and scoring notebook (we'll run in your VPC if requested).
- Benchmark run results (per-model token cost, latency p95, EM/ROUGE-L, human adequacy summaries).
- Recommendations: model + quantization + caching settings for pilot.

Attachments we are sending now
- claritywell-benchmark-template.csv (CSV template for the test set schema)
- redwood-eval-guidelines.pdf (scoring definitions and human annotation instructions)

Action items (proposed owners & timeline)
1) Claritywell: confirm dataset privacy level (PHI: yes/no) and expected ready date for initial 1k rows — Alex/Maya — by Wed 24 Mar.
2) Redwood (Ben/Priyom): prep eval infra options (hosted vs. VPC) and a high-level cost estimate — by Thu 25 Mar.
3) Claritywell: share procurement contact and PO window for a pilot; Alex to loop in procurement — ASAP.
4) Redwood (Priyom): once we get dataset, we'll validate format and run a small smoke test (50 rows) within 48 hours.

Next sync: propose a 30-min follow-up on Tue Mar 30 to review onboarding blockers and confirm final dataset. If Friday works earlier for you, we can move.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
[Attachment: claritywell-benchmark-template.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: redwood-eval-guidelines.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alex Thompson <alex@claritywell.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery — Claritywell eval kickoff

Thanks Kim — this reads exactly how I interpreted the call. A few clarifying questions before we move to dataset prep: 

1) Metrics: for the human adequacy 1–5 scale, can you share a short guideline (examples of 1 vs 5)? Will Redwood run the human reviews or do we provision annotators?
2) VPC vs hosted: we prefer everything to stay in our VPC due to PHI. Is that supported for short eval runs or does that require the Private deployment onboarding?
3) Timeline/cost: rough ballpark for a 1,000-row run (including human review) so I can tee this with procurement — our target is to complete the run and review by April 15.

Procurement contact: procure@claritywell.com (I've looped them on a separate thread).

Alex

Alex — quick answers inline: 

1) Human adequacy guidelines: Redwood can run the human review for you (we use a HIPAA-ready annotator partner for PHI or we can accept your internal labels). We will send a 1‑page rubric with examples (will attach once final).

2) VPC support: short eval runs can be run inside your VPC with our Private Eval mode (no Persistent Private deployment needed). That requires a short onboarding (network peering + credentials) and an SOW addendum for air-gapped handling — Priyom will follow up with the tech checklist.

3) Cost ballpark for 1,000 rows: $3k–$8k depending on models selected and human-review depth. If you choose hosted and non-PHI path, lower end; VPC + HIPAA partner pushes to higher end. I'll put a short estimate in the pricing doc and share a link.

If you want an official quote for procurement, we can produce a one-page SOW + estimate once you confirm dataset sensitivity and preferred infra.

—Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Tech details: dataset format, scoring script & smoke test plan

Hi Alex / Maya — technical follow-up from our side with specifics so your engineering team can format the payload correctly. We've included a small example in the attached CSV template. Key points: 

Dataset format (CSV) — required columns:
- id (string)
- prompt (string)
- expected_response (string) — anonymized canonical answer for automatic scoring where applicable
- category (string) — triage: diagnostic, medication, policy
- phi_flag (boolean) — true if PHI present
- notes (string) — optional context/links

Annotation & human review guidance:
- Human adequacy rubric (1–5): 5=accurate, clinically safe, concise; 1=incorrect/misleading or unsafe. We'll attach example judgments.
- For PHI rows we mark them and route to the HIPAA-ready annotator; Redwood will not store raw prompts outside your VPC if Private Eval is selected.

Scoring script (what we'll run) — outline:
1) Normalize model output (lowercase, strip punctuation except clinically significant tokens).
2) Compute EM and ROUGE-L vs expected_response where applicable.
3) Collate human adequacy scores; compute averaged adequacy and percent unsafe flags.
4) Produce per-model CSV and a combined dashboard with latency/cost per token.

Smoke test plan:
- You provide 50 representative rows; Redwood runs all selected models and returns raw outputs + scoring within 48 hours.
- We'll validate format, tokenization edge-cases, and whether caching affects prompts with long contexts.

Recommended model runtime configs for pilot:
- rw-instruct-13B: batch 4, seq_len 512, float16;
- rw-chat-7B-q4: batch 8, seq_len 512, q4_0 quantization (cost-focused).

Attachment: claritywell-benchmark-template.csv (sample 10-row file) and the Redwood eval guide with annotation examples. Please confirm three things so we can proceed: 
A) Does the dataset contain PHI rows? (yes/no + estimate %)
B) Which models from the list above you'd like in the 1k-run (pick 1–3)
C) Confirm target completion date for the run (you mentioned Apr 15)

If helpful I can share a short sample scoring script snippet — below is a minimal normalization we use: 

# pseudo-normalize (for reviewers)
# text = text.lower().strip()
# text = re.sub(r"\s+"," ", text)

Thanks — Priyom

Please confirm you can run the smoke test inside our VPC (Priyom mentioned Private Eval mode) and we'll open the onboarding ticket today. Also confirm an estimated total cost range (Ben) after VPC handling is priced in so procurement can finalize.

If all good we'll drop the CSV tomorrow morning and request the smoke test. Aim to have the smoke results back by Mar 28 so we can iterate before the full run.

Alex
